chief_complaint: thick cottage-cheese discharge and vaginal itching
hpi_details: A 32-year-old female presents to the clinic with thick cottage-cheese discharge and vaginal itching. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: She thinks she developed a severe allergic skin reaction after recently switching to a new scented body wash.
concerns: She is worried that the symptoms mean she has contracted a sexually transmitted infection from an unfaithful partner.
expectations: She hopes to leave with a targeted prescription cream or single-dose pill that will stop the intense itching immediately.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Vulvovaginal candidiasis (yeast infection) evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Vulvovaginal candidiasis (yeast infection) is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management uses topical azole therapy when pregnancy is possible or confirmed; oral fluconazole is an option only when pregnancy has been excluded, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Vulvovaginal candidiasis (yeast infection).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Bacterial vaginosis without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Recurrent infection may suggest diabetes or immunosuppression.

boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

teaching.one_liner: Patient with thick cottage-cheese discharge, vaginal itching, and associated fatigue consistent with a yeast infection.
red_flags: Recurrent infection may suggest diabetes or immunosuppression

must_ask.say: Can you describe the discharge and how severe the itching is?
Have you had yeast infections like this before, and how often?
Do you have diabetes, or have you taken antibiotics recently?

must_ask.objective: Ask about sexual activity and partner symptoms
must_ask.say: Is your partner having any similar symptoms?
We'll first check whether pregnancy is possible; topical antifungal cream is preferred in pregnancy, while an oral option may be suitable otherwise.

history.answer: I've had this terrible itching down below and a thick, chunky white vaginal discharge that has been bothering me for the last few days.
It started about four days ago with mild itching, but it has gradually gotten much worse over the last two days.
No, I have never experienced anything like this before; this is the first time.
It looks thick, white, and clumpy, almost like cottage cheese or curdled milk, and there is quite a bit of it.
No, there is really no foul or fishy odor at all, and having intercourse didn't change the smell.
The itching around my private area is intense, and the outside skin feels swollen, raw, and irritated.
My period isn't due for another two weeks, but the itching seems to have peaked over the past couple of days regardless of my cycle.
I do feel a slight burning on the outside skin when urine touches the irritated area, but no burning inside my bladder or urethra.
No, I haven't noticed any bleeding after sex or any spotting between my periods.
No, I have not had any belly pain, cramps, or pelvic aches.
No, I haven't had any fever, chills, or body sweats.
I tried having intercourse two days ago, but it felt quite sore and uncomfortable at the entrance because of the irritation.
I have been in a monogamous relationship with my husband for four years, and we do not regularly use condoms since we are trying for a baby.
No, my husband has had no discharge, itching, rash, or burning when he urinates.
I took a seven-day course of amoxicillin for a severe sinus infection that finished about one week ago.
No, I don't have diabetes, and I haven't taken steroids or any other immunosuppressants.
My period is regular and not late, but since we are not using contraception, there is a possibility I could be pregnant.
I take daily warm showers and use mild body soap, but I don't douche or use scented feminine washes. I do wear synthetic leggings often to work out.
We don't use birth control pills or an intrauterine device because we are planning to conceive.
My last routine Pap smear was about one year ago and was completely normal, and I finished all three doses of the HPV vaccine in college.
I feel more tired and run down than usual lately, probably because I was fighting off that sinus infection last week and haven't slept well from the itching.
I started using a new heavily fragranced body wash last week, so I thought my skin was just having a bad allergic reaction to it.
I cannot stop worrying that this is actually an STD and that my partner has not been faithful to me.
I just really hope you can give me an effective prescription cream or pill today to stop this unbearable itching.
I have never been diagnosed with any chronic medical conditions or gynecologic problems.
I had my wisdom teeth removed five years ago, but no other surgeries or hospital stays.
I am not taking any prescription medications right now, just an over-the-counter prenatal multivitamin once a day.
I don't have any known allergies to medications, foods, or latex.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used electronic vapes.
I drink one or two glasses of wine socially on weekends, but I have paused drinking recently since we are trying to conceive.
I work as a graphic designer and live in an apartment with my husband.
My parents are healthy, though my mother has high blood pressure; there is no family history of gynecologic cancers or diabetes.
My last menstrual period started exactly two weeks ago, and my cycles are usually very regular every 28 days.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 118/76 mmHg, pulse 72 beats/min, respiratory rate 14 breaths/min, body temperature 36.6°C, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Alert, comfortable in appearance, in no acute distress.
Abdomen is flat and soft without distension, surgical scars, or visible rashes.
Soft and non-tender across all four quadrants including the suprapubic area, with no palpable mass.
No rebound tenderness or involuntary guarding anywhere across the abdomen.
Erythema and edema of the labia and vulva with excoriations from scratching, without ulcers, sores, or vesicle clusters.
Speculum reveals copious adherent thick white cottage-cheese-like vaginal discharge and vaginal erythema; bimanual exam reveals no cervical motion tenderness and no uterine or adnexal tenderness.
